_reviewProof: 2026-08-01: proof of review moved from hand-written marker files to the RECORDED ledger. A marker is a separate act of writing performed by the party being audited â€” twelve such writes were flagged as forged in Butlery on 2026-08-01, and every stricter spelling of the assertion (name the file, pin the sha, list what you read) was still an assertion. In ledger mode a PostToolUse hook records which reviewer read which bytes and a SubagentStop hook records the verdict it ended on; nothing is hand-writable, and a later fix silently un-proves the file it touched. This repo's four agents already pinned shas honestly, so this is a hardening rather than a repair. All four carry the two rules it depends on: open files with Read, and end on REVIEW-VERDICT: pass|fail (N blocking).

reviewGates._note: BIN-757, 2026-08-06 (Malin's call in the backlog review): the last three patterns were added because the gate's shape was 'where does sensitive code LIVE', and the bulk-write paths live in components. A one-word comment change under functions/ earned a security review while the CSV import â€” which writes hundreds of watchlist docs per run, on the client, under the user's own credentials â€” earned none. 2026-08-09, BIN-830: added the .test.mjs pattern. The repo grew real .mjs test files (BIN-802) that this gate matched none of: docs/org/route.test.mjs, scripts/check-workflow-map.test.mjs, scripts/check-public-env.test.mjs. Its other patterns are deliberately repo-wide rather than src/-anchored, so the .mjs siblings belong at the same breadth. Deleting or weakening a gate's test is the same hole as deleting the gate. Note the two under scripts/ are ALSO outside vitest.config.ts include globs today (only 'docs/org/**/*.{test,spec}.mjs' and 'functions/scripts/**' are listed), so npm test never executes them -- which makes a named reviewer the only thing looking at them at all. Widening only; nothing was removed.

The whole-diff, cross-file pass. Was `codeReviewGate` until 2026-07-31, i.e. gated on the /code-review BUILTIN â€” a command only a human can start, so every unattended run (sprint-parallel, /commit, any resume) dead-ended asking Malin to type it. Same filePattern and same marker as before; the only change is that a spawnable agent now owns it. /code-review stays available and is still the deeper pass â€” it is simply no longer the ONLY way to earn this marker.
reviewGates._note2: 2026-08-08: added `^\.github/(workflows|actions)/`. Before this, NO gate in this repo covered the release path at all — a change to `deploy.yml` (which builds and deploys production), `preview.yml`, `ci.yml` or `secret-scan.yml` reached zero reviewers. Meanwhile `.claude/rules/deployment.md` already lists `.github/workflows/**` in its auto-load `paths:`, so the repo's own prose treated it as load-bearing while the automated half — the one that actually runs — did not. Two sources, opposite answers, and the automated one wins by default. Found by sweeping all three repos on 2026-08-08 after the same gap was fixed in Synat (BIN-820), where the identical widening (BIN-667) had already been made and this repo never got it. These are REGEXES, not globs: a literal `.github/workflows/**` throws `Nothing to repeat` at `new RegExp()`. `actions` is in the alternation even though this repo has no `.github/actions/` yet — Synat learned that gating only `workflows/` exempts logic the moment anything is extracted into a composite action (BIN-666/667), and the cheap time to cover it is before that move, not after.
reviewGates._note3: 2026-08-09, BIN-830: added the pattern matching exactly docs/org/route.mjs, docs/org/route.test.mjs, scripts/check-workflow-map.mjs and scripts/check-workflow-map.test.mjs. BIN-805 (24f6612) taught the ADVISING router (docs/org/route.mjs, TOOLING_CODE_FILES) that the router and the workflow-map linter ARE code; this BLOCKING gate was never widened to match, so a commit touching only route.mjs reached zero reviewers -- the self-clearing hole the ticket was filed about. Two lists decide who reviews a change and widening one never widens the other; keep them identical and grow both in the same commit. Deliberately scoped to those four paths and NOT to docs/**/*.mjs + scripts/**/*.mjs as the ticket text proposed: the narrow list is Malin's 2026-08-08 call (alternative (a)), and route.mjs carries a golden selftest asserting scripts/gen-app-icons.mjs stays tier skip -- a broad glob would make the blocking gate contradict a decided routing. Same shape as cd8c59e (.github/). Widening only; nothing was removed.
reviewGates._note4: 2026-08-12, BIN-851: added THIS FILE and .claude/rules/accepted-deviations.md. BIN-830 one level up, and that level decides all the others: no gate pattern here could match `.claude/shared-plugin.json`, so a commit that DELETES a reviewer pattern reached zero reviewers and convened no panel -- the gate could disarm itself unwitnessed. accepted-deviations.md is in for the mirror-image reason: it decides what a reviewer is forbidden to flag, so appending to it silently retires a finding class. Deliberately NOT `^\.claude/rules/.*\.md$` as the ticket's second criterion floated: lessons-digest.md is appended by the fold-back step of every single sprint close-out, and putting the integration reviewer in that path would gate routine bookkeeping on a review -- the same narrow-over-broad call Malin made for BIN-830. Also added to docs/role-responsibilities.md Sec 25 (Engineering Manager / Release Manager owns the process and the quality gates), so the ADVISING router stops answering `skip` for this file; both lists moved in one commit, per the BIN-830 lesson. Widening only; nothing was removed.
